utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-14/2-T, the Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Before we begin, there's a matter I want to deal with, with the Senior Legal Officer. There are matters of administration. [The Presiding Judge and the Senior Legal Officer confer] Mr. Nice, just one matter which concerns the trial before we go on with the witness. I'm sorry to have kept you waiting, General. There are some administrative matters which we're having to deal with, but we'll start your evidence as quickly as possible. I think we left matters, when we had our Status Conference, that there was a possibility that we'd be starting the Defence in May. That may have to be reconsidered. The work of the Trial Chamber, the overall work of the Trial Chamber, is under consideration, and the position is by no means resolved in the way we thought perhaps it had been last week. So I'm saying so that nobody should be under the misapprehension that there will be a long break. There may end up by being a shorter one. But as soon as we have definite answers, we'll try and let you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And of course, we know, as the Chamber explained, that consideration is being given to breaking the hearings of the Defence and, obviously, the earliest we can know about that the better --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- for all sorts of reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That is the matter under consideration, and it may be reconsideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: I'd like to throw our egg in when we have a chance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If there's something you want to say briefly, say it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEIN
utterances.text: The short of the story is the longer you can give us between the close of the Prosecution's case and the opening of our case, the shorter our case will be. That's the short version of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We left off last week looking at a video which was defective to the extent that it had no soundtrack. The Chamber expressed some concerns as to the value of the video or at least that part of the video that dealt with the interview of a soldier, because the witness wasn't able to say whether this was the particular video he had himself seen. The video now does have sound. The position is that the video will be laid before the Chamber either through this witness, or if the Chamber rejects that, as part of the material on international armed conflict for it is to that issue that it goes. I don't press the issue of whether it should be played now. I'm entirely in the Chamber's hands. It's through this witness it would be only of value in that it is similar to if not identical to the video that he had himself had seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It perhaps fits more naturally into another part of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It can come as part of international armed conflict and will be presented as part of the materials there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll hear it then or see it then.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it will have to be added to that body of material because it had formally been counted as part of this. But we'll remember, I hope, to deal with that. May the witness, see, please, Z45,1, which I think is in the stack of exhibits that the Chamber already has. It's the identity card of a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: General Merdan, what, if anything, can you tell us about this document, please?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I was given this document by a member of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. According to that member of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Ivan Sarac was killed in the Brod area between Tisovac and Podolci. And from what I know, his grave is there and a monument has been erected to Ivan Sarac who was killed there. His military document shows that he was a member of the army of the Republic of Croatia. I can also document it with a photograph of the monument which was erected there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In the summary, we go to paragraph 41. Did you represent the BiH side in the Busovaca Joint Commission?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I did, yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You can answer any further questions from my learned friends about that. What, if any, knowledge did you have prior to April the 16th, 1993 of the HVO's position of large-calibre artillery?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I knew that the HVO had large-calibre artillery, and I knew about that since the late -- since late 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Where was that artillery situated?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Those artillery weapons were in the territory of the municipality of Vitez, or better said, near the quarry which is between the Vitez and Travnik municipalities, and I think that that particular area is part of the Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May the witness please have map 2781,2 again before him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In May of 1993, were you given some responsibility for an aid convoy destined to go to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. As the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps, I was issued the order to escort a convoy due to Tuzla from the area of Gornji Vakuf to Novi Travnik, and then from the village of Sivrina Selo to Zenica, and then onward to Tuzla within the 3rd Corps area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can you just point out on the map and then just tell us what, if any, difficulties or obstructions you encountered?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In the area of responsibility where I escorted the convoy, that is, the 3rd Corps area of responsibility, I took over the convoy in the village of Bistrica, Gornji Vakuf, and I escorted it -- I followed it to the village of Opara or, rather, the village of Trenica near Novi Travnik. And from Novi Travnik to the village of Sivrino Selo, I don't know what happened to the convoy. When I took over a part of the convoy -- you cannot see the village of Trenica on the map. It is not shown here where I left the convoy, but you can see the -- you can see the village of Sivrino Selo, when I took the convoy over again or, rather, a part of the convoy, the one that had managed to get through to the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What should have happened between those two places? Who should have escorted the convoy?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That territory between the villages of Trenica and Sivrino Selo, through that area the convoy was to be escorted by the Croat Defence Council because that was an area where my life was in peril.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You having left the convoy at the one village and positioned yourself at Sivrino Selo to meet it again, how had you got from one place to the other, as a matter of history?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: From the village of Trenica towards Sivrino Selo, I took -- I walked -- I used mountain paths towards an area called Mescema, Travnik, Ovnak, to Sivrino Selo. That was the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Part of the convoy arrived at Sivrino Selo. What did you discover about the part of the convoy that did not make it?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In Sivrino Selo, I learned from the drivers who made it to Sivrino Selo that the convoy had been attacked by the Croat Defence Council. Their lorries showed signs or, rather, damage from light weapons. The drivers were very sad. They were crying. They could not believe that it could have happened. As for the part of the convoy which did not make it to Sivrino Selo, I really do not know what came to pass to it. I suppose it stayed somewhere in the area controlled by the Croat Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In September 1993, paragraph 44, did you express your views on the Geneva Peace Plan?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I expressed my view about the peace plan, yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What was your view as to its possible rejection?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I was really doing my best to implement on the ground all the peace plans agreed at the highest level, and I tried to see the agreement enforced in practice. However, in practice, we failed in implementing the peace plans, particularly when it comes to the joint command, the joint operations against the Serb aggressive on Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May the witness see Exhibit -- or at least have before him Exhibit Z1226. Your Honours, there are limits, of course, to the value of the testimony of one witness on the document of another. This particular one is an ECMM report upon which the witness's comment might be valuable. I think I'll probably avoid putting in the others that are in the stack. 1226,1. If that's laid on the ELMO, please, as it's in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: General Merdan, I'm going to read a passage under an entry of the ECMM and just ask whether this is an accurate description of your position at the time. It reads: "HCC met Mr. Merdan and discussed the implications of the rejection of the peace plan. He said the peace negotiations must continue. When asked if the BiH might sign an agreement after further territorial gains from HVO in Central Bosnia, he said it was possible but such a peace would not last. He stated that the Geneva plan was fundamentally flawed, as it insisted on ethnically-pure republics. He went on to say that the attempts of Mr. Abdic to establish an autonomous province in Western Bosnia was motivated by individual gain and doomed to failure." Does that accurately reflect your view at the time? If not, please comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nice, could you -- before the witness answers, could you tell the Chamber, which Geneva plan are you referring to? What plan are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I would try to get the witness to help us at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Which plan were you referring to here, General Merdan?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Mr. Izetbegovic and Mr. Mate Boban had signed an agreement on the situation in Central Bosnia, deciding to set up a joint command to resolve the conflict between the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Croat Defence Council. It is true that the peace negotiations about which we learned in a third 3rd Corps command, we commented on them, and I believe then and I still believe and I'm positive that in that territory or even beyond it, there cannot exist any ethnically-pure territories. It is quite obvious that in the areas controlled by it, the HVO wanted to create ethnically-pure territories, and this has never happened in the history of mankind, and that is why I firmly believe that ethnically-pure territories cannot exist. And regardless of the situation which prevailed at the time, I tried to arrive at a peaceful solution in that area so as to bring the number of victims to a minimum, and I thought that any attempt to create an ethnically-pure territory was doomed to failure from the start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Nice. I should like to ask the witness, General Merdan, the plan which was signed by Messrs. Izetbegovic and Mate Boban and your reaction to it, could you put a date to it, an approximate date to the plan and the time when you reacted to it?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I cannot recall the date when the agreement was signed, because the Commander of the 3rd Corps received the information about the so-called packet link. And as for that peace treaty or, rather, the agreement between Izetbegovic and Boban, I saw that through the packet link. A document referred to the establishment of a joint command and an attempt to put an end to the conflict between the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Croat Defence Council in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The ECMM passage that I read out then, does that accurately reflect your views at the time?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: It does accurately reflect my views.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 45. Don't give the substance of this until I've explored with you the route by which you learnt of the information. Towards the end of 1993, did you learn something -- don't tell us what -- from a military observer of what that observer had seen close to the front lines of Santici and Sivrino Selo? Just yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: As related to you by the military observer, was he telling you something he or she saw himself or was it something that had been relayed to him or her?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I cannot recollect what the observer told me at the time exactly, and I don't know how he learnt about what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The information coming to you from that observer, how fresh was it in terms of was it something that had happened the same day, the day before, or weeks before?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I don't know which information you're referring to, but I had contacts almost on a daily basis with representatives of the European Monitoring Mission and of UNPROFOR in the area. So could you please clarify which report you're referring to? Then my answer would be clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. Something concerning Kordic, but don't tell us what the content was for the time being.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: A representative of the monitoring mission told me that he had seen --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... When he told you what he told you, was it fresh information or was it something that was already days old or can't you recall?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure that it's going to take us much further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can the witness see, please, 1147,, please? This is an organigramme dealing with the BiH 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Do you have a few comments on this, I think by way of amplification or correction? We look at the centre of the document, coming down from the top, "Hadzihasanovic" and then your name, and then -- first of all, your name has been misspelt. It should be "Dzemal." The next name, I think, M-a-h-m -- what's the next letter? Should it be an "U" or a "Y"? Yes.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: "L". It should be"L". Dzemal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: "Sakib" is Sakib?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: "Majmoljin." In stead of an "N" there should an "L," "Majmoljin."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And two names down it should be "Dugalic," not "Dugavic"?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. "Ramiz Dugalic," "L".

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If you look, please, to the right of the list below that, right at the right-hand side where it's just got a "X," what can you tell us should be there, if anything?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That could be a command of the 3rd Corps with units attached to the headquarters and linked to the command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Is the organigramme otherwise broadly accurate?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: It is mostly accurate, only here we have an indication of five operative groups, whereas the 3rd Corps had four operative groups rather than five in this period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Finally, can you, please, from your experience, tell us what was Kordic's role in politics or military matters in Central Bosnia at the time you dealt with him, please?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In my deep conviction, and I have presented a number of examples here in the Tribunals, is that Dario Kordic had an exceptionally important role both in political life and military affairs in the area of Central Bosnia, particularly when important decisions were being made, and it is my opinion that Dario Kordic was the key figure at the time in the political and military life of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You will be asked further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A few technical adjustments, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: General Merdan, may I introduce myself. My name is Naumovski, an attorney from Zagreb. I'm one of the Defence counsel for Mr. Dario Kordic. I've few questions for you. Before I start, some customary advice as we know each other well and understand one another well. I'm sorry. Please wait a few seconds until the interpretation has been completed, and I shall be patient and wait for the interpretation of your answers before going on. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: A few introductory remarks first. As stated at the beginning, you graduated from the military academy in Split. You graduated there at the naval academy in Split, did you not?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Your entire career in the former JNA was served mainly in the naval/military area, as it was known then, and one of your last duties was in the brigade of rocket vessels or gunships, something like that, in Split, was it not?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. Before leaving the Yugoslav People's Army, I was in Split, in the brigade called the Rocket Brigade, rocket-armed gunships and boats, and I think I was there until sometime in July, when the command was transferred to the island of Vis.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Quite. That was the time when the JNA was preparing its attack on Croatia or, rather, the beginning of the war in Croatia, because it was roughly at the end of the summer in '91 that the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. There were combat operations ongoing in the Republic of Croatia already, and the JNA had already started combat operations at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You left the JNA sometime in November 1991 by mutual consent, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. I left the Yugoslav People's Army at the end of September 1991 and not at the end of November 1991, and it wasn't by consent. I was released. I had asked to be relieved earlier on, but I was not granted permission.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. But we can agree that you left the JNA after the war was well under way in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. One could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Continuing this brief review of your career, if I understood you well, on the 15th of April, 1992, you became what was known then as the commander of the Territorial Defence of the district of Zenica, the former region of municipalities.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: The dates are not quite correct. It wasn't in April 1992. I wasn't immediately appointed commander of the district defence headquarters of Zenica. At that time on that date, I was a member of the district staff, and later on I became the commander of that district staff of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Can you perhaps give us a more precise date when you became commander of the Territorial Defence of the district of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. On Thursday, I think it was, you said that sometime in November 1992, you were formally appointed to the 3rd Corps, even though the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina actually started operating on the 1st of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The order was drafted in November on my appointment, and the command of the 3rd Corps started operating on the 1st of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You were later appointed deputy commander of the 3rd Corps. For what particular area of activity were you appointed? Did you cover a particular department, if I might put it that way?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Within the system of control and command, the deputy commander of a corps did not have any special area of responsibility like the other officers did. He was the deputy of the commander. He stood in for the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. A few more questions regarding the period between the time when you left the JNA and your activities as deputy commander of the 3rd Corps. Upon leaving the JNA, you were in contact with Meho Karisik, I think his name was -- he was your teacher in Split, I think -- regarding, as could be seen later on, the question of the establishment and foundation of the Patriotic League. I don't think we need go into any details, but this is just a broad question. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. At the end of 1991, I got in touch with Mr. -- he is now deceased -- General Meho Karisik, who was my teacher for a time at the naval academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: This Meho Karisik was appointed commander of the Patriotic League headquarters, formed sometime in August 1991, was it not?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was appointed commander of the Patriotic League, but he did have an important role in the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: My final questions regarding the Patriotic League. On the 7th, 8th, and 9th of February, 1992, in a village called Mehurici in the Travnik municipality, a military congress of the Patriotic League was organised by Sefer Halilovic and a number of other people. That military congress of the Patriotic League was held in the house of Fikret Ajanovic, and that was actually the first military consultation of regional commanders of the Patriotic League for the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. At the time, a consultation was held of the commanders of the Patriotic League for various regions of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I cannot remember exactly the name of the owner of the house, but I know where the house is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The place of Mehurici is known in the Federation as one of the main strongholds of the Mujahedin forces, with quite a number people coming to settle from outside Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I don't think that is quite correct. There are no Mujahedin forces there, but it is inhabited by mostly Muslim people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But to round off this set of questions on the Patriotic League, since you are from Busovaca, I assume that you know that a detachment of the Patriotic League was formed at the time in Busovaca as well. The commanders were Dervis Sarajlic, Senad Ekmescic, somebody Abdulah Muminovic, and I don't know the other names.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. There was a detachment -- not really a detachment, because "a detachment" means a large number of people. A group of founders of the Patriotic League did exist in the territory of Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: General Merdan, your rank is Brigadier- General and you are Assistant Defence Minister of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina for personnel, are you not?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. I am a Brigadier- General of the Federation's army, and I hold the position of Deputy Assistant Minister. So I am Deputy Assistant Minister for personnel, not Deputy Minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. But before that, you were head of the department for military education in the Bosnian component headquarters of the Federation army?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. Before that, I was Deputy Assistant Minister for the inspectorate in the Defence Ministry, and before that I was head of the department for military education in the Ministry of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. You made a statement to the investigators of this Tribunal in February 1995. That was the one and only statement that you gave to the investigators, not counting the interviews you had here?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. It was then that I made an official statement for the Judges from The Hague. At least that is how they introduced themselves at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Were you a witness in any trial that is being conducted against Croats in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but primarily I'm referring to the area of Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. This is my first testimony of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: During the time of the war, did you keep any kind of diary?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I did not, but I did take note of events on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you do have some notes that you took regarding events that you considered to be important?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. What I had time to take note of, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I assume you reviewed those notes before you came to testify here. Do you have them on you, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I do have them on me, but for certain reasons I have not had time to look into them in detail. I had some private obligations to take care of.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you didn't have time to study them, but you did review them in the interim from '95, when you made your statement to the investigators, to the present?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I did review them, but I didn't study them closely.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Were only official data taken note of in those notes, that is, things linked to your official duties?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I took note of what I saw, experienced, and had time to take note of.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. That's what I meant. What I was going to say, there's nothing in those notes of a private nature, of a personal nature, relating to family matters. They relate exclusively to official things.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, no. These are notes. It is not a diary so there are private and personal things in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Let me ask you now a few questions about the relationship of Mr. Blaskic and Mr. Kordic within the frameworks of the examination-in-chief. The first of those topics would be what you said relating to the fact that Mr. Kordic stood in for Colonel Blaskic at the tripartite talks held in December 1992 at the airport of Sarajevo. Do you remember what you said about that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember very well what I said. The only thing I'm not sure of was that it was in December of that year, but, otherwise, that was how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You personally, General Merdan, were never present at any tripartite talks which were also attended by Mr. Kordic on the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I was not present at that kind of negotiations, but I was present at other negotiations between the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Croatian Defence Council, which was also attended by Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. We'll come to those later. But I'm now focusing on these negotiations at Sarajevo airport. If I understood you correctly, General Merdan, you don't really know the real reasons for General Kordic substituting for General Blaskic at those negotiations?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I'm convinced that I do know the reasons. I tried to convey them, because Dario Kordic was not satisfied with the work of Filip Filipovic, who is also a Brigadier-General today, and he dismissed him from his position. And on a number of occasions I had the opportunity to see that Dario Kordic would take over the initiative and make the decisions whenever something important had to be decided.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I understood what you said, but please listen to my questions and answer them briefly, because in that way we will save time. I just ask you whether you agreed with what I said, and that is that it is merely an assumption on your part why Kordic replaced Blaskic at that meeting; that is, because of his dissatisfaction with Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that is an assumption but based on previous reactions of Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know at all who proposed that Mr. Kordic, together with Ignjac Kostroman, substitute for Colonel Blaskic at the talks at Sarajevo airport?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know that Colonel Blaskic himself asked he be replaced at those talks?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I never spoke to Tihomir Blaskic about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wanted to show General Merdan an exhibit, D52/1. However, since the General has agreed with me that this was just an assumption on his part as to the reasons for the substitution, I don't need to show him the document. It is a letter by Colonel Blaskic, in which he proposes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. You told us, General Merdan, that Colonel Blaskic, on a number of occasions, was unable to make decisions and then Kordic made them. How do you know that? I did not hear or, rather, Their Honours haven't heard a single concrete example of that.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In my testimony, I said this on a number of occasions. When I was captured and arrested. Also, at meetings at which Blaskic was present and Kordic was absent, Blaskic could not always make a decision on the spot, especially when the decision was important. I said that he always had to consult somebody, and my assumptions are based on what I personally experienced and saw, and I spoke about those things at some length.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Correct. You did speak about those things, but you said that he had to consult somebody, and as far as I understood you, we assumed that he did consult someone. But you yourself said that you know that his superior was the commander of the HVO headquarters, Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic. So he may have consulted him. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In the system of control and command, Milivoj Petkovic was portrayed in that way, the way you have put it, but I think that in practice, it was not always the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Let us not debate this any further. I have my opinion; you have yours. But would you agree with me that you do not, in reality, in concrete terms, know who Blaskic consulted on any of these issues?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. I do know that regarding specific issues, Blaskic consulted Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Give us an example, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: An example is my arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you have any other example apart from your arrest?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. I do not have any proof, because I do not know who was at the other end of the line and how the conversation went with Blaskic when Blaskic was talking with someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Let's move on. Once again connected to Mr. Kordic -- I'm continuing my questions on that subject -- you mentioned that sometime in January 1992, you say that there was a celebration of the electoral victory of the HDZ. Mr. Kordic made a speech in Busovaca, at a meeting there. Do you recall that event?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I saw a tape which was filmed at the time. It was a videotape which exists in the archives. But I was not present in the hall in which Kordic made his speech, but there is a videotape in the archives of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I agree with you on that score, yes. However, it was not the celebration of an electoral victory of the HDZ, because the elections took place in 1990, in November. This was another celebration which took place in Busovaca to celebrate the recognition of Croatia as an international state, an internationally recognised state, and this was on the 16th of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I cannot recall the date, because I wasn't present, as I said. But I did say that I saw the videotape which was filmed on the occasion, and I would like to see the tape again so that I can confirm whether I had seen it or not, if that is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: General Merdan, you told us here that on that particular tape, the one that you have mentioned, and that is the only event that took place in January 1992 where there were a lot of people gathered for a celebration, there weren't any other events, I can assume that we're talking about the same event, and you say that Mr. Kordic stated something to the effect, "We're going to live now in a common state, in one state, a single state, the State of Croatia." That is the gist of your quotation. I would like to ask you the following: Are you quite certain that that statement was made by Mr. Kordic himself?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic, on several occasions, spoke of --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting you, but I'm just talking about that particular date, January 1992, not any other events. That particular date.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I saw the videotape. I did not have occasion to see it again, but it does -- but Dario Kordic's speeches were intoned in that particular manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, but at that meeting he did not state that. Another speaker said that, not Mr. Kordic. That is what I am putting to you.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, we can look at the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the tape was shown. It was Z2699.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have the tape. We've seen it. And rather than relying on secondhand evidence about it, we'll rely on the tape itself. There is no need to continue the questioning on this particular matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. That is precisely what I myself wished to propose.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So we can skip that bit now and move on, General. Mr. Kordic and some events in Busovaca, that's what we're going to talk about. You mentioned the takeover of the barracks, the Draga barracks in Busovaca. That took place on the 26th of April, 1992. You were present on the occasion. You were in the courtyard, I believe. Do you recall that, General?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember the event. I was near the courtyard; that is to say, near the barracks and the courtyard that you mentioned, in that particular period.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: There were a lot of people there, were there not? However, nobody, except an official delegation, was allowed to enter the barracks, but this duty was only assigned to the commission, the JNA on the one-hand side and the other party, the representatives of the Croats and Muslims from Busovaca who were to take it over. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with you. The decision, I suppose, was taken by somebody else, but the decision of the wartime presidency at which I was presented did not take that kind of decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Who was the leader of the delegation who was to take over the barracks to represent the Busovaca side, if I can put it that way? If you remember, of course.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: While the war presidency was in session, I cannot recall exactly who said that the barracks were already being taken over, but from the meeting of the war presidency, at the time the legal organ of power and authority in the Busovaca area, we moved towards the Draga barracks, and at the head of this team was the president of the wartime presidency, Mr. Zoran Maric. He led the group. When we came to the barracks and wanted to enter, the soldier there did not allow us to enter. He was a soldier of the Croat Defence council. And I noticed inside Dario Kordic, who was in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I've already said that there were a lot of people from Busovaca present because this was an exceptional event, because it meant finally the JNA would leave the area. But what I wanted to ask you, in fact, is whether you know -- perhaps I'm going to remind you of this in asking my question -- that the president, if I may call him that, of that joint delegation which took over from the Busovaca side, this particular barracks, was Mr. Florijan Glavocevic. He signed the minutes and he escorted, if I can use that term, the JNA as they were leaving the Busovaca area. Have I jogged your memory somewhat?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, this event took place later on. You are speaking about our arrival in front of the barracks, and my own arrival in front of the barracks. What you're talking about is another event. They are two different events which took place on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. If I have made a mistake I do apologise, but I think it took place at the same time you were there, when Mr. Glavocevic toured the barracks with somebody else -- I don't know what his rank was but he was a representative of the JNA -- in blue uniforms, and he took over the barracks. I'm thinking about that event which took place in the early hours of the afternoon on the 26th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, I'm just telling you about what saw when I was present. So I'm talking about the wartime presidency meeting and the arrival of the war presidency on the spot. I was refused entry into the barracks as a member of the war presidency. Now, who toured the barracks later on, these facilities, I wasn't able to see because I wasn't able to enter the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well then. I have just one more question in that regard. Do you remember at all whether Mr. Florijan Glavocevic was there wearing a civilian suit and a tie? If you don't, say so.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that Mr. Glavocevic was wearing a civilian suit and that he was not in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you, General. You have been using the term "war presidency." In fact, it was not a wartime presidency, if we have in mind the same body of authority, and I can only assume that we are thinking of the same organisation. The municipality elected what was called a crisis staff. So what you mean, in fact, is the crisis staff led by a Croat, the former mayor Zoran Maric. And his deputy was a Muslim, the president of the executive board of the Municipal Assembly of Busovaca Mr. Asim Sunulahpasic. I think that you have in mind that particular body.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, I think it was the war presidency at that time, that it was called the war presidency of the municipality at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't want to confuse Their Honours. The war presidency was established by the Muslim side in Kacuni in January 1993, whereas this particular organ was called the crisis staff. And that is where the difference lies, if I may remind you of that. But never mind. Whatever it was called, it was this joint body with the representatives of both the Croats and Muslims within it, the legal authorities in the Busovaca municipality. That is the organ we have in mind.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: The organ that I am thinking about is the one that had constitutional provisions which allowed it to make decisions, and Mr. Zoran Maric was at the head of that particular organisation. So it was not a staff, it was a body having the right to make decisions according to the constitution that prevailed in Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time. So I am talking about the legal organ of parent authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But I would like you to agree with me when I said a moment ago that Zoran Maric's deputy was Asim Sunulahpasic, because it was a joint body, was it not?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a joint body, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Let us move on to another detail once again linked to Mr. Kordic. You said that in January 1993 you heard that somebody had filmed a tape of some kind with a telephone conversation, and you say that you recognised the voice of Dusko Grubesic. Do you remember that particular detail?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When you heard and recognised the voice of Dusko Grubesic, what duty did Dusko Grubesic perform at the time; do you know?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: As far as I know, at that time he was commander of the brigade of the Croatian Defence Council for the Busovaca municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You said the following, literally, when you spoke on Thursday: "I think that on the other side of the line, thinking of the conversation, that it was Kordic, but I'm not quite sure"?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you do not know who was on the other side of the connection, you only assume that it could have been Mr. Kordic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's what I said on Thursday, and that's what I'm saying today as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's proceed. We have several more questions in relation to Mr. Kordic. You know the family, the Kordic family from Busovaca, I assume, the mother, the father. Mr. Kordic is a younger member of the family, but I assume that you know the Kordic family, in general terms.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I had occasion to become acquainted with the Kordic family, the mother and father. But, in fact, I did not know them well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, all right. That's what I meant, but you knew them. I assume that you know where Mr. Kordic worked before, that he was a journalist in the Vatrostalna company, he was a journalist writing for several papers, and, in fact, he graduated as a journalist. Did you know that, General?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I know that Kordic worked in Vatrostalna, but what particular job he had there, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you also know that Mr. Kordic, in the former state, had no military training, he had not completed any military schools, so he did not have any military knowledge and education, in fact?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I did not know whether Dario Kordic had any military education or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, very well. But you didn't hear of him having any later on, did you? I assume you didn't.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear this from anybody ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. As we're talking about Mr. Kordic, do you know, in precise terms, and I'm going to remind you of some details, what duties and when Mr. Kordic -- what duties he performed and when he performed them? And I'm talking about the time after the first elections. For example, do you know when he was exactly President of the HDZ in Busovaca, when he was the Deputy President of the HDZ for Bosnia-Herzegovina, and so on?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I don't know these terms precisely, these dates precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you know or do you know that Mr. Dario Kordic was the Deputy President of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna from the 18th of November, 1991, to the 28th of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of those dates, but I do know that he was Deputy President of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know -- do you happen to know how many Deputy Presidents the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna had?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. I did not study that question; nor was I interested in it; nor am I interested in it now, in knowing how many Presidents it had.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic, from November of 1992 up until after the Washington Agreements, that is, 1994, he was the Deputy President of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you happen to know how many Deputy Presidents of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina there were in that period?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. Here we are debating matters which the General has said, in relation to a similar question, he doesn't know. It's of no assistance to the Trial Chamber, really, to know what the state of knowledge of a witness such as this was. We will be able to hear, in due course, your evidence about this particular matter. So I suggest we move on to other topics.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I accept that. But I should like you to understand that in view of the assertions General Merdan is making, I must see whether he knows something more than what he has said. But I agree. I shall move on, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: A moment ago you talked about the situation in Busovaca. May we agree that the President of the crisis staff, or whatever we like to call it, and he was President of the municipality of Busovaca before that, that is to say, Mr. Zoran Maric; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. I did say that, and I think that the order by which I was arrested and prohibiting the legal organs of authority, in one of the points of that order it states that the decisions of the wartime presidency are considered null and void, and this was signed by Dario Kordic. I don't think it says "decisions of the crisis staff." I think it says "of the war presidency." And the original order exists in the army archives of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I have submitted a copy to this august Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you also happen to know that that same individual, Zoran Maric, was President of the HVO of the Busovaca municipality from August 1992 onwards?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I believe he was, yes, because in the municipality the Croatian Defence Council was proclaimed, and in an order dated May 1992, this became visible, that is to say, that the HVO was being established, and so I assume that Mr. Zoran Maric was appointed to that duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, he was appointed, but he was appointed in August. Up until August, for several months Mr. Glavocevic performed that duty. Did you know that, perhaps? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: After the conflict at Kaonik, I was no longer present at meetings of the war presidency, so I do not know whether that duty was later on performed by Mr. Glavocevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, we can move on, related to Mr. Kordic. One of the individuals with whom you connected with Mr. Kordic was Anto Sliskovic, and asked by the Prosecution, you said that, in fact, he was responsible to Mr. Kordic for his work, something along those lines. And your conclusions are based on the signing of a statement after you were released from detention. It is Z101,1. Do you recall that, General? The signature here is Mr. Sliskovic for the regional staff at the bottom. Do you know what the regional staff represented at that time, regional headquarters? And I was talking about May 1992, in that period.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In that particular month, I was arrested. They did not wish to release me, and I spoke about that in some detail, although a very strong, respectable delegation of the parliamentary members of Bosnia-Herzegovina insisted upon my being released, and within that composition there were the representatives of the Croatian people. And on that occasion, Sliskovic said that I could not be released without authorisation from Dario Kordic. The representatives then proceeded to contact Dario Kordic, and according to their statements he was located in the Tisovac area at the time where he had his forward command post. And on the basis of that, we were able to conclude that Sliskovic could not have released me without the authorisation of Dario Kordic, and then we can go on to deduce that Dario Kordic made the decisions as to what Sliskovic would do. And in my statements, I confirm this, the ones that were published for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, we're going to go back to that later on, but you haven't answered my question. What was the regional headquarters, in fact, in May 1992, immediately after the Serbs launched the attack in the region, the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, I have already said and I can say so again that I never entered into the substance of HVO organisation. At meetings, I always wanted to look towards the joint aggressor on Bosnia-Herzegovina who was well defined at the time, so I did not deal with organisational matters linked to the Croatian Defence Council because I considered that it was not my place to do so. I am only saying what happened in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this in a different way. The period you're talking about, was it before General Blaskic established his headquarters for the whole Operative Zone in the village of Kruscica, and that was in June, July, August 1992, that is to say, before the military headquarters was set up?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, you're talking about the period of May, May/June, and I said that in October, I think it was 1990, but in the autumn of 1992, that is, I was at the headquarters in the village of Kruscica, and this was at the Lovac Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, we agree, then, that what we are talking about was before the Central Bosnia Operative Zone led by General Blaskic was formed. Do we agree on that point?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In May, as far as I know, to the best of my knowledge, General Blaskic did not assume that post.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But do you happen to remember that in May or thereabouts, Filip Filipovic, today also a general of the army of the Federation, dealt with matters of military organisation and resistance to the JNA on that territory?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that. Colonel Filip Filipovic at the time introduced himself as colonel. I do know him, and on several occasions he contacted us in the district command of the Territorial Defence. And at a briefing which was held in Zenica, Filip Filipovic said that he could not stand up to Kordic, because it was our idea to set up a joint command in the Lasva River Valley, and the proposal was that Filip Filipovic should be the commander of that Operative Zone and I myself, as a Bosniak, should be his deputy. But Filip was not able to accept that because he told us at the meeting that Dario Kordic did not agree with that concept. And I think that afterwards, as far as Filip told me, there was a verbal exchange and conflict in the conception for combat operations in Central Bosnia, and Colonel Filip Filipovic was replaced and Tihomir Blaskic replaced him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So we can agree that Filip Filipovic at that time was in charge of giving shape, if I can say that, to the resistance to the aggression which took place in that area at that time?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, we can agree, for that particular time period.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I now have five or six questions linked to the arrest of Mr. Merdan, so perhaps this would be a good time to take a break, rather than going into that question, because I won't succeed in getting through it. But if you wish to, we can continue, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, that sounds like a convenient time. What kind of progress are you making now, Mr. Naumovski, with the witness? How long do you anticipate being?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In view of the topic in hand, I haven't got through a great deal of material. I do have quite a number of questions left, but I'll do my best to finish as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Would you keep that in mind. We have several other witnesses who we need to hear this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Merdan, let us resume. We were about to talk about your arrest in Busovaca in 1992. You mentioned document Z100.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, could the witness please be shown Z100, in the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: It will be easier for you if you have it before you. While we are waiting for the document, could you tell me who was it that interrogated you while you were in Busovaca? You know people in Busovaca, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: They were relatively young people.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you don't know their names, do you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I know that one of them was called Svabo, tall, fair, but they took shifts in front of me. And who was behind me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But do you know the names of people who beat you, as you described it to us?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I could not see who was beating me, because I was facing the persons sitting in front of me. So I could not see who was hitting me behind my back, because they would not allow me to turn.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Will you please be so kind and look at this document Z100. You are a soldier, I'm not, but I've seen quite a number of such documents. It has the form of a military order, and then there are various items saying what one should do, what one shouldn't do, and so on and so forth. Do you see the signature at the bottom of the document? It is the commander of the municipal staff of Busovaca -- can you see that --"Ivo Brnada"? And on the right-hand side there is Dario Kordic's signature. Do you know it for certain that Ivo Brnada was indeed the municipal commander of the HVO headquarters at that time in 1992? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But would you agree with me that this is in terms of the structure? You must have seen a whole series of military orders issued by the HVO, but this is an HVO order in terms of its structure, in terms of the commander, and so on and so forth. The commander will always sign on the right-hand side. I suppose it was the same thing in the army of the B and H.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Any army, any organisational structure will structure a document in a specific manner. As a military man, I know there are instructions as to how military documents should be structured. What I see here, is it says that it is an order, and it is evident that this is an order which was signed on the right-hand side Ivo Brnada, and on the right-hand side by Dario Kordic. Likewise, as a military man who spent all his life in the army, and all the armies the world over, there is no dual leadership or dual command. One is the order written by a commander of a relevant unit, and he then will sign his own order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. But will you please cast a look at these items at the beginning of the document, the third, the second, rather, the third and the fourth, which refer to the TO. Let me speed matters up. It says that the TO should lay down the weapons. The TO must replace under the HVO command and so on. Now, my question to you, as a man who then came to command the Territorial Defence in the Zenica region, the TO never laid down its weapons, rather, hand over its weapons to the HVO, did it, as this order said?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Which region do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I mean the region covered by this order. The municipality of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: While I was in the area, before my arrest, the Territorial Defence did not hand over its weapons. But did they do that after I was arrested? I don't know. However, I received information that the HVO was seizing the armaments, the weapons that could be found in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you will agree with me that the TO established its own command at Kacuni, with their own men and weapons and so forth. Of course, people lived in Kacuni and went to work regularly. What I'm trying to say is after the order, after this order, the TO continued to operate in the territory of the municipality Busovaca in spite of this order.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: The TO existed according to a decision of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the Bosnia-Herzegovina ordered that all the units should be placed under the command of the Territorial Defence. Needless to say, some of the Territorial Defence units existed also in the territory of the municipality of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So this ultimatum that we read in this document never came true in practice, did it, because the TO continued to function?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. This order was implemented throughout the municipality of Busovaca in full, and for the most part in all the areas controlled by the Croat Defence Council. So the order was enforced in full.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Let me rephrase it differently. Would you agree with me when I say that the administrative borders of the municipality of Busovaca at that time were divided between the TO and HVO interests, spheres of interests, that there were two spheres of interest?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: There was no division before the conflict. After the conflict the division did take place. Please allow me. I wish to point out, in front of this august Chamber, the Territorial Defence units were focusing on the aggressor against Bosnia-Herzegovina and along the front lines facing the aggressor. And as I said it last time. Here were only men who were taking a rest, because we did not have enough weapons to arm all the men who had been organised in the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, right. We are now moving on to another topic, and we shall come back to it later. So let us try to round off this part, the part that relates to the time of your arrest. You mentioned that a delegation from Zenica had arrived, and one of the members of the delegation was Mehrudin Saltinovic [phoen], a Muslim, and then Dr. Barac, a Croat, and some other people. Was that the delegation that you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And after that delegation arrived and had talks in various places around the municipality of Busovaca -- Your Honours, this is not in dispute -- this delegation also met and talked to Mr. Kordic also. So when we're talking about this delegation, that delegation did indeed come there, and after a round of talks in the municipality, you were released, and I think you were only in detention about two days or something. I don't remember what you said.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I need to mention here that the delegation which is mentioned here had talks with Dario Kordic. Dario Kordic decided not to let me in, not to admit me there, so the delegation came to my father's house, where I was staying at the time, and informed me that Dario Kordic would not release me. So they conducted some consultations, and Mr. Dominik Sakic left the delegation. He went to a place called Tisovac, to Dario Kordic's headquarters, which was guarded by uniformed soldiers. And when he came, he told the delegation that Mr. Franjo Boras was with Kordic in Tisovac and that Dario Kordic nevertheless decided to release me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Let us just confirm what you just told us. You heard it from Dominik Sakic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Dominik Sakic told the whole delegation that was in my parents' house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Your Honours, we naturally disagree with this last sentence uttered by General Merdan, that Dario Kordic opposed or did not oppose. Dario Kordic, and that is how we put it, Dario Kordic heard what happened to General Merdan from this delegation for the first time, and he asked quite a number of people to find facts about what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Now, General Merdan, I have just one more question.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I wish to intervene. I disagree with the counsel, because a day before that Mr. Bruno had been to see me when I was in detention and said that Dario Kordic would not allow them to set me free, and I want you to call this witness in relation to my arrest. Susnja, he is Bruno Susnja. His name is Bruno Susnja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, we've gone over this now. Let's move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one more question. It is very important, and with this, I will finish this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But, General Merdan, you will agree with me, won't you, that when you came home after you were set free, you were in your father's house in Busovaca, and will you agree with me that Mr. Florijan Glavocevic immediately came to see you in your house, that is, in your parents' house, and that he expressed his regrets about what had happened to you, that he came immediately to see you, and that was the first time that he had heard about that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Even before that, Florijan Glavocevic was aware of what had happened to me, because he was in contact with the military or, rather, the civilian police of the Busovaca HVO, and that is where we had the first contact. So Florijan Glavocevic did know what had happened to me. He may not have seen my back, but he was quite aware of what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you didn't answer me. Did he, indeed, come to visit you in your house and express his regrets? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What does it matter, as far as Mr. Kordic is concerned, whether Mr. Florijan gave any regrets or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because Mr. Florijan Glavocevic came to express his opinion and convey Mr. Kordic's opinion, that is, the astonishment of what had happened to Mr. Merdan. That is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Did Mr. Florijan say anything like that to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But was he in your house?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Glavocevic was in my house. But, Your Honours, I wish to state some other facts here, which are two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: General, could we please concentrate on the point. Did Florijan pass on the regrets of Kordic? That is the simple point.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Florijan Glavocevic did pass it, but whether he had indeed said that, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Let us now talk about your second arrest. In autumn '92, Darko Kraljevic arrested you in Vitez. That is what you said. We shall not go into that again. We know that at your request, you were brought to Mr. Blaskic's headquarters. Would you agree with me that you absolutely do not know who it is that Colonel Blaskic spoke over the phone from a room which was not the room that you were in?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: What I wish to say is that it was not my second arrest but one in a series of arrests to which I had been subjected. I do not know, that is quite true, who Tihomir Blaskic called to consult, but I pointed out repeatedly that when Dario [sic] Kraljevic's units arrested me and took me under custody, whenever I showed that pass issued by Tihomir Blaskic, they would not let me go. But when I showed the permit issued me by Dario Kordic, then they always released me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But, General Merdan, don't make it more difficult for me. We shall waste too much time. I asked you very specifically. Right, perhaps one of the arrests, but I'm talking about the arrest by Darko Kraljevic and what happened in the room on the premises of the Operative Zone of Colonel Blaskic. My question was simple. You do not know who Tihomir Blaskic called to talk about your arrest, you said?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: True, that is what I said, and I said that I guessed it was Dario Kordic. That was based -- my assumption was based on the previous experience with him, and I explained it and showed it to this -- to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So that is only your assumption?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, because I did not see who he was talking to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Right, thank you. But if we're talking about arrests, in that series there was yet another one. In April 1992 you were detained. As a matter of fact, it was an ECMM delegation, representatives of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the HVO. There was Franjo Nakic, there was you, and I believe some other people from the ECMM. And you were stopped, I believe, by the head of the military police in Novi Travnik. Do you remember that particular incident? You spent about two or three hours there, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I was stopped at various roadblocks in Novi Travnik repeatedly and then taken into custody, so I do not know which incident you have in mind. Was it sometime in mid-April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Quite so. Your delegation, the delegation of which you were a member, was responsible for finding those four abducted HVO officers, and I think it could be on the premises of the military police in Novi Travnik or, at any rate, in some official premises.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember those details. It is true that we had set off to look for the abducted representatives or, rather, officers of the HVO from Novi Travnik, and we set off to look for those men at the site where they had been abducted. And the head of the European Monitoring Mission at that time on that commission was -- no, I can't remember the name, but I know that he came from Spain, and we were brought to a hotel in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: All I want to know, briefly -- and I was wrong. I referred to April '92. Of course, it was in April '93. But I wanted to ask you just one question in this regard. Who did that officer who detained you negotiate with over the telephone, and on whose intervention were you then released? I believe his name was Stipo Paraga [phoen]. It's just come to me.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, if I looked at my notebooks, I would also know the name of the man. It is quite true that the commander would not release me, but he did set free members of the European Monitoring Mission. But having learned from my previous experience, I asked representatives of the ECMM to stay with me, because I could only guess what might happen to me if I stayed there all alone. The commander would not let me go, and they spoke to Tihomir Blaskic. A representative of the ECMM requested that he speak to him personally, and I do not know what they talked about. But be that as it may, we had to wait long, until late hours in the night. It wasn't only a couple of hours, it was for many hours. I don't know who they talked to, because they spoke from a different room. But be that as it may, we were all set free after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And that was what I was going to say. This conversation that you just mentioned was with Tihomir Blaskic. That is what I wanted us to agree on.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, the first conversation was with Tihomir Blaskic, but that commander refused the orders of Tihomir Blaskic. They were waiting for consultations from somebody else. That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Let us now round off this part when we refer to Mr. Dario Kordic. You agree with me today about four or five things, when you confirmed to this Court that these are only your assumptions, your inferences, that you were not aware that Mr. Kordic was involved directly. But you involved Mr. Kordic, let him know the situations, and consider him responsible for this?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You seem to be making some arbitrary views. On the other hand, you showed that you dislike Mr. Kordic, in that you're trying to embroil him in everything, even when he has nothing to do with it?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I must disagree with this, because this is only a conjecture based on some facts presented by the Defence. I present a sum of my conclusions, inferences based on facts that I came across and which I showed to this august Chamber. So I cannot agree with this Defence's conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Naumovski, let's move on now. We really must make greater progress.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Inaudible] in relation to this document that you have before you, and these are the events in the then JNA barracks at Kaonik. The Chamber has already heard a great deal about this, so we shall go only briefly through it, as you also referred to it briefly. The crisis staff of the Busovaca municipality, which included Zoran Maric, Florijan Glavocevic, Husein Hadzimejlic, and Asim Sunulahpasic, and a number of other people, decided locally to distribute the weapons from Kaonik on a 50/50 per cent basis, isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: On the part of the TO, the duty was assigned to Husein Hadzimejlic to deal with this, whereas the Croatian side, in all these talks linked to the takeover of the barracks, was led by that same Florijan Glavocevic that we have referred to.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I think that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: However, in view of the structure of the JNA, the talks went on for some time, people went to Zenica, Besim Spahic was the town mayor at the time. Anyway, finally the JNA agreed to leave, and these two persons, Husein Hadzimejlic and Florijan Glavocevic, were to take over the barracks on the 9th of May, 1992 as representatives of the TO and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: The assumption may be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that apart from the local members of the TO, suddenly a large number of unknown people appeared, some from Zenica, others from Kacuni, and they -- some 100 men rallied on the side of the TO, and they were in front of the discotheque known as Leptir or butterfly.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean, Kacuni Territorial Defence, Busovaca Territorial Defence, or something else. I think you're mixing things. The Busovaca Territorial Defence had its units within the Busovaca municipality under its control. I cannot see that they can be considered outside units at Kaonik. It is also true that in the area under the control of the 3rd Corps or, rather, at the time under the control of the district staff of Zenica, there was the military police of the Zenica district staff, both in Busovaca and in other places which were in the area of responsibility of the Zenica district staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I simply wanted to point out -- that was the gist of my question -- that apart from the people known by the inhabitants of Busovaca, there were people unknown to them who arrived. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I would not. This was not a large group of people.
