utterances.text: Tell me, please -- I beg your pardon. I forgot about the interpreters. Was the area of Fojnica under the 3rd Corps, was it in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: For a certain time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The 1st and 2nd of July, '93, is my question.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The 2nd of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly now, but it is true that units of the 3rd Corps were deployed in that area. Whether this was so at that point in time, I can't tell you without looking into the reports which are in the archives of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very briefly, do you know that the town of Fojnica was proclaimed a zone of peace and that an agreement to that effect was signed in the presence of representatives of the International Community?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: This agreement, in the presence of the European Community, was one of many. I can't exactly remember that particular date when Fojnica was apparently proclaimed a town of peace.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you're a military man, so could you agree with me that at the beginning of July, a major offensive was launched by the BH army against the HVO and that thousands of Croats had to leave Fojnica municipality and the town itself, of course?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: You didn't say which year.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: At that point in time, I was not in the Fojnica area, I was elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: At the time conflicts had escalated?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't there at the time, I wasn't in Fojnica, so I can't confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: These were a few questions relating to the 3rd Corps, and you were the Deputy Commander, and that's why I think they're relevant, and that's why I address them to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with such a witness, one could go on forever with questions, but it is my duty to heed your advice, and that would end my cross-examination. Thank you for your patience, and thank you too.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I'm always at the disposal of this Honourable Tribunal. If necessary, I can go on testifying for any length of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Kovacic. I trust, General, we're going to finish today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll do certainly my best and I hope I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: General, my name is Bozidar Kovacic. I'm an attorney from Rijeka, and with my colleague Goran Mikulicic I represent Mario Cerkez, the second accused in this case. I should like to refer you to the advice given at the beginning regarding interpretation, but I shall ask to phrase my questions so that you can answer them in most cases with a yes or no. Of course, you realise that if certain clarifications are required, of course you will have a chance to do so in the

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: consider that to be absolutely necessary. Something that my colleague asked you about earlier on, but I think it is more or less clear now, regardless of the fact that you and colleague Naumovski did not agree on the name of the joint body which operated in Busovaca in the course of 1992 as being a joint body with both Muslims and Croats represented, you said it was a legal body that functioned in Busovaca in 1992. I know that. But answer with a yes or no if you know. Was that same model applied in other surrounding municipalities?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Specifically that would include Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Thank you. General, without entering into the dates of the formation of the army and the transition from the TO to the army, there's quite enough material in the record already about that. I think you mentioned it indirectly. Do you recall that in Vitez, in the town of Vitez, a celebration was held of the anniversary of the BH army on the 14th and 15th of April, and on one of those two days you were present as a representative of the 3rd Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Could you please give me the year?

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: I apologise. 1993. Just before the conflict. The 14th and 15th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I cannot recall, but the 15th of April is the day of the founding of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Possibly I was there, but I cannot remember just now.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: So you don't know any details, whether the celebration went on for two days or not.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the Registry, please, provide the witness with all the documents that I handed over earlier on. To abbreviate things, I will ask the witness to look at two documents. They are all attached together so that we can distribute them all to everyone without wasting any further time. The one I gave during the lunch break.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: General, would you be kind enough to look at the map first and keep the other documents aside. Put them to the side so they don't bother you. On the basis of data or, rather, maps provided by our learned friend the Prosecutor, would you please look at this map first? My first question: Would you agree that the blue dotted line marks the territory of Vitez municipality, as far as you were aware, of the administrative divisions? Does that correspond to your knowledge, the territory of Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Roughly, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Do you think that there is any major deviation on this map? I consider that it is quite possible there might be some minor corrections required, but what is essentially, I think, is correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: It is difficult for me to answer this question, because I do not know with precision the territory of Vitez municipality, but in rough terms, this does correspond.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Tell me. In green are the numbers of the brigades of the BH army. So those are units that have been mentioned as being present in this territory of Zenica, Travnik, Lasva Valley, and in some places, in the course of the conflict from April 1993 onwards, without entering into the situation prior to that date, they were in contact with HVO units that were operating in the territory of Vitez municipality. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: What is shown on the map is not correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: I'm not claiming that geographically this is correct. These were just units that were present in the area, in the broader sense. Can you confirm that those units existed in that area?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: The way in which you have indicated on the map, they did not.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Let me go on to my next question then. Tell me, General, regardless of their actual deployment, which is not important just now, they certainly had their own area of responsibilities. That's what you're referring to, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: So each military unit, when deployed in a certain area, has a designated area of responsibility. Can we agree?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, General, while we're still on this topic, you're a highly educated military man. You were certainly familiar with the JNA doctrine, of which you were a member during ex-Yugoslavia. Is it true that the Commander of every Unit must know two lower levels of the disposition of his units? If we're talking about a Corps, the Corps Command must know the deployment of the Brigades and deployment of Battalions. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That depends on the tactical situation.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. So in some situations this is correct. In others, it is not?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In principle, a Corps in any army does not go down to the level of Battalion. So the 3rd Corps didn't go down to the level of Battalion, only to the level of independent battalions, which were directly under the command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You can leave -- put the map aside. I don't think we'll need it any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could I have an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The map will be numbered D52/2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: In case this were to mislead, this witness, of course, has not accepted that the markings on the map represent the positions of units or anything of that sort. So we can simply admit it as a map, roughly, of Vitez municipality, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Mr. President. We will be coming back to that through a number other documents, but just to be sure I understood this correctly, I think the witness said that he didn't confirm such a deployment, the positions of those units. Can I ask him once again so that we can be sure?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. He said he couldn't confirm the deployment. So let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Mr. Merdan, General, sometime at the beginning of your testimony on Thursday you said that you were aware that Cerkez -- I beg your pardon. Let me ask you another question first to lay the ground first. In your testimony, when talking about various incidents, you mentioned various units that existed within the HVO in the territory of Vitez municipality. Is that correct, that there were several units within the territory of Vitez municipality?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Then you also told us that it is your belief that Cerkez, as the Brigade Commander, was responsible for the area of Vitez. We were just speaking about areas of responsibility. Did you know exactly what the area of responsibility was of the Vitez Brigade on the day the conflict broke out, the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: As far as I know, and according to information conveyed to me, the HVO was deployed in accordance with the territories of municipalities, and that is how their units were deployed.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: But, General, you just said as far as you know. Please, do you have any document or any specific report on the basis of which you can claim that the Vitez Brigade within Vitez municipality was responsible for the whole territory of Vitez or for a particular part of it? You do not have any such document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: The Brigade Commander is responsible for the area and, therefore, Mario Cerkez, who was a Commander of the HVO Vitez Brigade, and I consider him to be responsible for the whole area of Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Unless he had a clearly designated area of responsibility assigned to him by a superior command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: And you didn't see any written order from which you could infer that he was responsible for the whole area of Vitez municipality. You are basing your response on a model.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I'm claiming this on the basis of meetings with Mr. Mario Cerkez and meetings of the joint commission. At all meetings held in the presence of the European Monitoring Mission, Mario Cerkez claimed that he was responsible for those areas which were the subject of discussion at the meeting, and they were all on the territory of Vitez municipality and his area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: But after the 17th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, after that date as well.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: But not on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Before the 16th and before the 15th as well.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well, General. Let me ask you something else concerning areas of responsibility. The area of responsibility of the Vitez Brigade, until the beginning of the conflict in April 1993, was in quite a different position. It was in the area of Novi Travnik, on the front line towards the Army of Republika Srpska. You know that.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't there. The Vitez HVO Brigade was not there.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Is it not correct that they were west of Dzakovici which we can see on this map, that that is where they were deployed?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: For a time, the HVO Novi Travnik Brigade was deployed there.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: And the Vitez Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: And where was the Vitez Brigade, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: The Vitez Brigade was not deployed in that area, the Vitez HVO Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: So you're claiming that until the outbreak the conflict, the Vitez Brigade was not deployed in a sector near Turbe or, rather, Mount Vlasic?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. An HVO Brigade commanded by someone, I think his name was Nakic, was deployed there. That was his area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Are you referring to the first half of the month of March? Are you talking about the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: At this point in time I can't recollect the exact dates, whether it was from the 1st of March -- until the 1st of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: So let me put it differently. Regardless organisationally, to whom did they belong? Were there low-level units, battalions, or other units? Were they HVO members on the front throughout 1993, not to mention 1992, until the beginning of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That is possible. That is quite possible.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. But we'll be coming back to that later. As far as the 325th Brigade is concerned, of the BH Army, it had three battalions in the municipality area. And to shorten time, it was in Kruscica, Poculica, and Stara Bila; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. At that time the Vitez Brigade did not have three battalions. It had two battalions and other units attached to it.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: You mean the 325th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. We're thinking about the same brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. In Kruscica there was Mr. Hakija Cengic, if I am correct, when the conflict broke out; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: In Poculica there was Mr. Sivro Sifet; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: And if I tell you that in Stara Bila a Captain of the former JNA was there, Captain 1st Class by the name of Salkic -- I don't know his first name -- does that -- do you remember that? He should have been in Stara Bukve, in Bila?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. The 325th didn't have a battalion there, and I do not know the gentleman you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Then there was a MOS unit there which was in Kruscica under the command of Nesib Herum; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the MOS unit was not within the composition of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: In the 3rd Corps we had only one brigade with the prefix "Muslim."

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You mentioned this on several occasions; an officer in the HVO, Mr. Filip Filipovic, a well-known officer. And I'd like to ask you, General, whether Filip Filipovic, in the course of 1992, together with the BiH Army, co-operating with it, organised many operations in defending the territory against the Serbs; that is, in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Not many. He did some, but without co-ordination with the BiH Army; that is to say, without co-ordination with the Territorial Defence, because he did not wish to have co-ordination or probably he did not -- was not allowed to co-ordinate.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Let us mention some of the more important points, and I'm sure you'll remember that at least in some of these operations, co-operation did indeed exist. And I think that this is essential, because there must have been co-ordination. First of all, there was the operation at Slimena, when it was decided to take back the weapons of the Territorial Defence which the army had seized from the municipalities, and that was an operation led by Filip Filipovic. Cerkez was his assistant, and the forces of the HVO took part as well as the forces of the BH Army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: There was an agreement that we launch a joint operation, but we didn't do so because Filip Filipovic attacked the barracks without the knowledge of the command of the general staff of the Travnik Defence. So he attacked without their knowledge, so there was no co-ordination.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well, General. Filip Filipovic attacked the barracks with his forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: The Muslims joined in on the following day and took weapons with the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. So they divided up the bounty?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, they did not divide up the bounty. That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: You mean everybody took their own?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a free-for-all. Everybody took what they could.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. In June 1992, there was a large-scale operation to take over the barracks in Travnik, and the HVO, with Filip Filipovic, took part in that again; is that right? He was not the leader of that operation but he was there with the HVO units that he commanded; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: The operation was led by the BH Army, was it not?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: So it was led by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: They jointly led the operation.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: So there we did have co-operation and co-ordination; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, not fully, because Kordic did not want to have that co-operation. He entered the barracks himself and then took away the weapons that were to be found there. And thank God there wasn't an incident on the occasion; otherwise, there would have been many dead bodies.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: General, I'm now asking about Mr. Filipovic and I'm not asking about Kordic. We agree that Filipovic was the leader of that operation?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I say that there was limited co-ordination.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Let us mention some similar operations. And you tend to minimise them in your testimony, but I should like to remind you of the HVO role in the defence of the town of Jajce in the fighting of the 8th -- from August to November 1992. It is not true that the role of the HVO was a minor one, as you stated. The HVO held this, and the Vitez and the Novi Travnik people know this. There are documents about that. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: You mean after the fall of Jajce or before the fall of Jajce.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: I mean before the fall of Jajce, between August and November, and even after the fall of Jajce?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Before the fall of Jajce, according to my information, the HVO brigade of Jajce was up there. Now, whether people came from the HVO brigade in Vitez, I don't know. Possibly, they were there at the front lines. The possibility exists, but I cannot claim that that is so.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Thank you very much. After that, at Turbe in August 1992, there was another large-scale operation in the region near the Konak village in the Vocnjak region. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Once again, both sides, both armed sides, took part. Yes, there was an operation there, and the HOS Units were in the lead there, which I think were commanded by Holman. Mladen Holman was the Commander of that unit. I think Anto Prkacin was there as well at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: We'll go back to that, but on the HVO side there were different units, and Filipovic was in charge of co-ordinating them on the HVO side?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Probably, yes, he was in charge of co-ordination, but we did not effect co-ordination with Filipovic. We did so with HOS.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Next there was a line on the Vlasic Plateau, and it was Karagic, Kostolac, Galica, that was how the line ran, and in the Sesici region, they were Units of the BH Army, it was in September, so we knew the connection lines. So there must have been a joint plan, must there not? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: On the map, and I said that the units of the Croatian Defence Council held a small portion of the line of defence towards Vlasic, that is what I said earlier on in my testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: And do you know whether these were units from Vitez?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. It was the area of responsibility of the 2nd Brigade, and I do not exclude the possibility that members of the HVO from Vitez did take shifts.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Yes, that they had one-week shifts. On the sector Dzelilovac, Potkraj, Paklarevo in November 1992, there was co-operation there with the commander of Turbe with Mr. Sulejman Leko; is that correct, would you say?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Co-operation did exist but to a lesser extent, and we had problems there in having the unit pass through towards Jajce.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And so on and so forth. I'm not going to enumerate them. There were many other points. So you say that the co-operation was poor, but it seems to me that it did exist, and we agree there, don't we?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you to have a look at the documents that I gave you. First of all, not the first document that you have before you but the second one, the one underneath. Yes, that's right. The first three pages are in English, and then you have the Croatian text. It is Document 01237/93 of the 3rd of June, 1993. Could you turn to the last page, and the signatories are you yourself and Nakic. So from this document, we can see that there was co-operation for a joint resistance against the Serbs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes. We always aspired towards that goal, but we never realised it.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Tell me, please, for purposes of illustration, as we have this document in front of us, under point 41 on the second page, once again the need is asserted to determine the areas of responsibility, in this case towards the Chetniks, and then it goes on to define more precisely what that involves; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct that we would agree in this way, but nothing was done in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I have an exhibit number, please, for this document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked D53/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: General, if I might ask you now to take a look at the second document on the table. Once again, you have the English version first and the Croatian original version after that. I should like to draw your attention to the title and the introductory paragraph. It is a report from a joint meeting of the HVO staff and the BH Army in Vitez. It is at communal municipal level, signed by Sefkija Djidic, the number-one man of the BH Army in the Vitez municipalities, and the Commander of the Battalion that functioned in Vitez at the time, Mr. Anton Brkovic. From the introduction, you see that a meeting was held on the 18th of December, 1992. We see that the individuals present on the HVO side were the representatives of the HVO staff of Vitez, the Defence representative, Marijan Skopljak, and the Commander Petkovic who signed the document, and the officer of the battalion, Ivan Budimir. And on behalf of the BH Army, it was signed by Sefkija Djidic, the head of the command, and Sulejman Kalco, the Cmmander of 325th, Esad Dzenanovic [phoen], the Commander of the 1st Battalion of the 325th Brigade, and Hakija Dzelilovic, and so on and so forth. Therefore, there we see that we have the representatives of the 325th, that is to say, the units which functioned within the composition of the 325th Brigade in the area of Vitez, and the representatives of the municipal staff of the HVO. Once again, they agreed on different points. They informed each other about the formation of units. They set up a joint operative body for the defence of the municipality, and they assign tasks for the coming Christmas and New Year celebrations and holidays. I should like to ask you, finally, whether you, as a member of the command, the second man in the Corps, the number-two man, whether you received this report. Do you know about it? Are you aware of it?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Probably this report exists in the archives of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Do we agree that this is, yet again, an example of where a form of co-operation was attempted to have as best defence against the Serbs as possible?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, but this is only on paper.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Let me ask you in a different way, Mr. Merdan. Regardless of the quality of the co-operation, which quite obviously you're trying to minimise, that is to say, you consider that it was not sufficiently satisfactory, that the HVO and the BiH Army in the Lasva River Valley, had they not existed, how could they -- if they did not co-operate, would the Serbs not have taken over the area?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: The Serbian aggressor, had he been able to, he would have taken over the area, but they were stopped after Jajce and were not able to go forward.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: General, may I ask you, you say they were stopped, they were halted, so it was through the efforts of both sides, which according to the presidency decision was both the HVO and the BiH Army, regardless of whether one side was more deserving than the other for this?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: So you are telling us, General, if I understand you correctly, that the HVO role, in the defence of the Serb aggression in the Lasva Valley, was not essential at all?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That is not what I said, no.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Then I do not understand you, General. Could you explain it to me?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I'll try and explain it to you. We really did try to set up a joint command in a specifically difficult situation after the fall of Jajce, and I talked about this because the Prosecution asked me for an answer to that question. So in Travnik we established -- we tried to establish a joint command, and I spoke about an operative room where Dario Kordic was located in the building of the railway and transport company. It was the ZTO building. There was a hall where we would have our meetings, our joint meetings. And we went out to the front lines to dig fortifications, but the HVO did not go out to the lines. It did offer artillery support. So the HVO was in the second line of the defence, not in the forefront of the defence. And although he did supply artillery back-up and had strong weapons, the weapons that the HVO had, had we been able to unite them, quite certainly the Serbian aggressor would have done much less harm to Bosnia than they did do.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Please put me right, General. You are, in fact, criticising -- I'm saying the following: that the existing potential could have been used to much better effect than it was. Is that the substance of what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: The substance of your question a moment ago was whether or not co-operation existed in matters of defence. I say that it was very small, there was very little joint co-operation, and that the combat potential could have been put to better use had there been better co-operation between the command and the units of the BiH Army on the one side and the HVO on the other.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I don't know whether there is the same proverb in other countries, but we say it's easy to be a General after the battle. What you're saying is your analysis of the situation after the events had taken place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. It is my assessment and evaluation during that period and the events that took place at that time. I'm not a General after the battle. I'm a General before the battle, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Thank you. But I think that you will accept that other individuals, other officers, have other opinions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's pure comment. Now let's move on and get on with the questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: You mentioned, at the beginning of your direct examination, something. You gave us, that is to say, a brief history of how HOS was formed and how it developed, and you said that it was not equally represented in all parts of Central Bosnia. I should just like to ask you a brief question to clarify matters. You said that in Zenica, the HOS was placed under the control of the Territorial Defence, and you also said in this connection that after the beginning of the conflict, and I suppose that this was April 1993, that the HOS disintegrated in Zenica, it was dismantled, and that some of the members went to the Lasva Valley. Would you agree that some members of HOS from Zenica, when it dismantled, went to the Vitez municipality? Do you know anything about that, General?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: First of all, I should like to apologise to this august Tribunal to say -- in saying that I was a General before the battle. But now let me answer your question, the question that has been asked me. I do not have any information as to where the members of HOS went from the Croatian people who were in HOS in Zenica, the Croatian members.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. So you don't know. But you said yourself that they had gone to the Lasva River Valley area?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: To all intents and purposes, they had nowhere else to go but there.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we round up, in the HOS in Zenica, under Zeljko Holman's command that you mentioned a moment ago, there were 80 per cent Muslims, Muslim members, at one time. Does that correspond to your own information, General?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Whether it was 80 per cent or not, I don't know, but quite certainly there were more Muslims in the HOS units in Zenica than there were Croats from Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: But Holman left the Territorial Defence in 1992, did he not? I think it was sometime in September or perhaps October. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I cannot say. I don't know whether he left during that -- the HOS units during that time.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. According to this diagram -- and I'd like to ask the witness to be shown the diagram so as to avoid misunderstanding, Z2792 -- looking at this diagram which you have had before you three times already, according to the diagram -- and you question this diagram, and so do I, at least in certain sections -- Blaskic could not have given orders to Kraljevic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Could Blaskic give orders to Cerkez, according to the state of affairs on this diagram?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: He could have ordered Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, he could have. Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: I mean Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, Blaskic could have.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: But according to this diagram, it would appear that Darko Kraljevic could issue orders to Cerkez, were this diagram correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, you can't deduce that from this diagram.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: You mean because there isn't the little line leading downwards?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, the diagram that I have in front of him, I say, no, he could not have.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Very well. Look at the one-but-last line, that is to say, the line below "Nakic", or "Blaskic" because Nakic is just the deputy commander, but along that same line there, the line of the brigade, the Vitez Brigade under Cerkez' command, we also have two other boxes, one stating that there was a certain Anto Krizanovic and the other box with the name Nenad Santic. I'm, first of all, going to ask about Anto Krizanovic. You said that you did not take part in the compiling of this document?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I just commented on it.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: But as the commander in the area, did you ever hear of this individual called Anto Krizanovic as being the commander of anything?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I personally never heard of that, no.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Nor have we heard of it. So you know nothing about what that is supposed to mean. Thank you. I'd now like to move on to the next topic. General, could you please tell me whether you were informed of the fact that when you were arrested on the 14th of April, 1994, in Travnik -- you told us about that today during the direct-examination -- you said that at your request, a representative of the ECMM remained here because you had a very bad experience with all of that, but I should like to remind you, and please tell me what you think about it: On the occasion, Mr. Franjo Nakic was with you, was he not?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Well, "unfortunately" is not the right term to use.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Well, I apologise. That was ironic. I was speaking ironically. But Franjo Nakic was with you, was he not? Perhaps you haven't --

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, I've understood the question. I'm just trying to remember, because I see that you think that it is very important. I do not think Franjo Nakic was there with me then, but I cannot say for sure.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Perhaps I can refresh your memory, and then you'll be able to give us a yes/no, answer. When the military police arrested you -- Stipo Dvorka, that name was mentioned, I know it was that particular individual -- on the occasion, Nakic expressly stated, he said to the policeman, "Then you can consider me under arrest as well," because he cautioned them that you were there as a negotiator, as member of a joint commission. Does that refresh your memory to any extent?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, it could have been that way. Perhaps it was. I cannot say hundred per cent, but there were other witnesses there. And, please, if it is important for the Court, there are also the interpreters of the ECMM, there were the drivers of the ECMM, there was a man from Spain who led the team, and perhaps you should ask other witnesses about it. If it is of such paramount importance, then you should ask them. I'm not really sure. There were times when Mr. Franjo Nakic behaved very correctly. Yeah. Right, right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: General, I don't know what the point of all this is. What is the point, Mr. Kovacic? What are you trying to establish?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I was about to come to it. The point is that the brigades could not control the military police and yet they came to visit their brigade. So I had to lay the foundation to my question.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: At the end of the story about the arrest and all this detention, it all took several hours. And during all those contacts, negotiations, the local Brigade Commander and Franjo Nakic told you explicitly that they did not have and had no authority over the military police and apologised because they felt embarrassed by this whole incident. Could you confirm this or deny this or is it that you don't remember?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I don't remember the detail. It was a long time ago. I simply do not remember.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Thank you. That is quite natural. General Merdan, you will agree, won't you, that after the conflict broke out between these two sides, between the Croat and Muslim or, rather, between the HVO and the BH Army in the Lasva Valley, started before that in Novi Travnik in 1992, in Busovaca in 1993. In Vitez, however, the conflict had not broken out yet. There were some incidents, but there was no serious major clash between the two sides. Would you agree with that? Just yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't agree with that statement.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: So you do not think that is correct. Right. You mentioned that in October 1992 there was a meeting or, rather, meetings which were attended by General Praljak from Croatia. It is not said anywhere, but that must be quite clear, that all these meetings had to do with the position to be taken in the war against the aggressor, that is the JNA, and local Serbs; that is, co-ordination of joint operations of the Army of BH and HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That is what General Praljak said.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: But these were not the commissions -- negotiations to deal with peace, to settle disputes between Bosnians and Croats, no?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: So the only question there was the defence?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: The joint defence.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. The agreement -- one of the agreements was mentioned, and you said that the units outside the Lasva Valley. The term, the expression "units outside of the Lasva Valley" meant the HVO, the Croat troops. But isn't it true that in a series of peace agreements throughout 1993, especially those concluded by the joint commission, the local commission with the headquarters in Nova Bila, they always referred to units outside -- they always meant all units of both sides outside that area proper. So if the agreement was being reached at the municipal level, then units outside the municipality, if it was at a high level, again units outside that particular region. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: So you think that whatever agreement of this whole host of agreements, units mentioned outside the area should move further away and that refers -- that means only the HV.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: I still repeat that I did not see the Units of the Croatian Army. I saw individual members of the Croatian Army, but I saw videotapes -- men who had been captured, affirming that they were members of the Croatian Army and Croatian Units. But those who were captured had not been captured in the territory of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: They were people from Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No. Six Croat soldiers, whom I released in Gornji Vakuf, had come from Central Bosnia. One of them said that he was a member of the Croatian army, and he had come from Osijek. That is from the unit called Osijek, which was part of the Croatian Army.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: But you have no document to know that he was, as such, in Central Bosnia, even as an individual?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Yes, because Blaskic told me to release them because the traffic was stopped, everything was blocked. And I was arrested then. I was arrested by the HVO Commander Sebesic, his name was, or Cobanac, I believe he was called, and at that time I really had major difficulties in getting through to Gornji Vakuf to release men who had started from Central Bosnia to Herzegovina; that is, Croatia.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. At the commission sessions, the HVO insisted on the units moving out of the area, and explicitly it is mentioned here -- let us not go through a million documents here -- both the Krajinians and the Mujahedin, and so on and so forth. Those units were mentioned. Is it true that the HVO insisted that they be moved away when the ceasefire is signed? Would you please be accurate about the date because that is important. As of April 1993.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: As of April 1993. In April 1993, the 17th Krajina Brigade was founded, that is true, but not the Mujahedin detachment. And the seat of the 17th Krajina Brigade was in Travnik for the major part, even though it was a manoeuvring Brigade, but headquarters and their relatives or refugees were in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: They had come from Cacin [phoen] Krajina to that area.

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR
utterances.text: But what part of Bosnia did they come from?

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: They came from those areas when they were expelled by the Serb aggressor. The Commander of the Brigade at that time was Fikret Cuskic, and he arrived from the territory of the Republic of Croatia where he had served with the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, could you please tell the Court -- because it is now ten past 4, and we really should organise work -- how much longer do you think you will take to cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I'm quite sure that I could finish within half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, you must do so, because you've had 50 minutes already. Your client was barely mentioned by this witness. Yes. We'll adjourn now. Mr. Nice, are you going to be very long in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I've got several questions, most of them acceptable to yes and no answers. I usually don't take very long in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You have a witness waiting, I expect.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I have two witnesses waiting for tomorrow. Perhaps fortunately, as it were, one of them is recovering from flu, and I think he's quite content not necessarily to be started tomorrow. Then I've got another one for the following day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. A final exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document that was submitted, the report dated 18 December, 1992, will be numbered D54/2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: General, I'm sorry that we have not been able to complete your evidence today. I must ask you to return tomorrow, please, at half past 9, when we will finish your evidence I hope in fairly short order so that you can get away.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May I make one point --

utterances.speaker: DZEMAL MERDAN [RESUMED]
utterances.text: Whatever you order me to do, I shall comply with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I was only going to make one point about an exhibit, better made today while it's fresh in our memory than put off to extend the cross-examination; that is, the article from the Washington Post that was read out. The only passage that was read out is what other sources said about the witness. I couldn't object at the time, not having the document in my hand. It appears from the Washington Post that the passage was never put to him, and none of the witnesses' quoted observations or answers were relied on. So its value as a document seems to be very limited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You could deal with it, if you want, in re-examination, as far as necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: While we're talking about exhibits, let me clear this up. There's -- 2463.4 was a transcript which was handed in, which I don't think we're going to need.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: That's correct. That goes with the video that we didn't use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: So we can hand that back, can we? Please. And likewise, a document has found its way onto my desk -- perhaps we better deal with it tomorrow -- called "Structure of the HZ-HB, 1992-1993." I don't know where it comes from. Perhaps we can deal with it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I think that's a document provided in the Status Conference pursuant to a request or discussion about the desirability of having an organigramme generally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We can discuss that in due course. 9.30 tomorrow, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
